posts.content:
🌍 HOW TO BUILD A JOB-READY RESUME AND FIND INTERNATIONAL JOB OPPORTUNITIES FROM HOME
🚀 Your next career opportunity could be global. Is your resume ready?
In today's competitive job market, having experience and qualifications is not always enough. Your resume must clearly communicate your skills, achievements, and professional value to recruiters and hiring managers.
Whether you're a fresher, an experienced professional, a career changer, or someone aspiring to work overseas, the right strategy can help you stand out.
Here are some essential tips to strengthen your resume and improve your international job search.
📌 1. Create a Job-Oriented Resume
Avoid using the same resume for every application. Analyze the job description and highlight the experience, skills, and achievements most relevant to the position.
📌 2. Write a Powerful Professional Summary
Your summary should communicate who you are, your experience, your core expertise, and the value you bring to an organization. Replace generic career objectives with specific, role-focused statements.
📌 3. Showcase Achievements, Not Just Responsibilities
Instead of writing, “Responsible for preparing reports,” explain how you improved reporting processes, saved time, or enhanced accuracy. Use genuine metrics wherever available—never invent results.
📌 4. Optimize Your Resume for ATS
Use relevant keywords naturally, maintain clear headings, and choose a simple, professional, machine-readable format. The goal is to make your qualifications easy for both recruitment technology and human reviewers to understand.
📌 5. Build Evidence of Your Skills
Projects, certifications, portfolios, and practical work samples can strengthen your application, especially if you're a fresher or transitioning into a new field.
📌 6. Explore International Opportunities Strategically
Research employer career pages, LinkedIn, international job portals, remote positions, and visa-sponsored opportunities. Always verify location eligibility, work authorization requirements, and the legitimacy of employers.
📌 7. Strengthen Your LinkedIn Profile
Keep your headline, About section, experience, skills, and portfolio aligned with your resume. Build professional relationships with recruiters and hiring managers in your target industry.
🎯 Remember: A 90% job-match score is a useful personal benchmark, not a universal ATS guarantee. 
Genuine skills, relevant achievements, and a well-targeted application matter more than an arbitrary percentage.
Your career deserves a strategy, not just another application.
💬 Are you planning to apply for international jobs? What is your biggest challenge—resume writing, finding opportunities, or getting interview calls? Share your thoughts in the comments.
Repost this to help someone take the next step in their career!

WE ARE HIRING | Desktop Support Engineer – L1

📍 Location: Gurgaon
🏢 Work Mode:Work from Office
🌙 Shift: Night Shift
💼 Experience: 1–3 Years
💰 Salary: Up to ₹3 LPA CTC

ClickTooFly is looking for a skilled and proactive Desktop Support Engineer – L1 to join our growing team. The ideal candidate should have hands-on experience in desktop support, IT troubleshooting, networking, and dialer support/administration to ensure smooth day-to-day IT operations.

Key Responsibilities:

* Provide L1 desktop and technical support to employees.
* Troubleshoot hardware, software, operating system, and network-related issues.
* Install, configure, and maintain desktops, laptops, printers, and other IT equipment.
* Provide support for dialer systems, including login issues, call connectivity, audio issues, and agent configuration.
* Monitor and troubleshoot dialer-related issues to minimize downtime and ensure smooth calling operations.
* Assist with dialer user/agent creation, extensions, configurations, and access management.
* Configure and troubleshoot LAN/WAN, routers, switches, access points, and VPN connectivity.
* Handle Windows installation, updates, patching, and system configuration.
* Manage Microsoft 365, Outlook, OST/PST files, and email-related issues.
* Provide remote support and maintain IT asset and incident records.
* Escalate complex technical issues to the relevant teams whenever required.

Required Skills:

* 2–3 years of experience in IT support/Desktop Support.
* Hands-on experience with dialer support and troubleshooting.
* Knowledge of Windows OS, hardware troubleshooting, and system configuration.
* Basic networking knowledge, including TCP/IP, IPv4/IPv6, LAN/WAN, routers, and switches.
* Familiarity with Microsoft 365 and Outlook configuration.
* Strong troubleshooting, communication, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work independently during night shifts.

What We Offer:
✅ Competitive salary
✅ Career growth opportunities
✅ Dynamic and supportive work environment
✅ Opportunity to work with a growing travel company

📩 Interested candidates can share their updated resumes at:
hr@clicktoofly.com

author.about:
As a senior finance and treasury professional with over a decade of progressive experience, I have built my career around delivering strategic value through effective cash management, foreign exchange risk mitigation, and financial planning. My expertise lies in designing and executing treasury strategies that drive operational efficiency, ensure liquidity, reduce financial risk, and align closely with business goals.

Currently, I serve as Treasury Manager at Airtel Kenya, where I oversee multi-million-dollar FX operations, manage debt portfolios, and lead high-impact financial initiatives. One of my most notable achievements includes spearheading a $250 million de-dollarization project that reduced foreign currency exposure by 40% within a year—an initiative that earned me a fast-tracked promotion. I also developed and executed a full USD hedge policy that enhanced cash predictability and protected the business from currency volatility.

Previously, as Head of Treasury at Java House Group, I led company-wide treasury operations, significantly reduced bank charges by 80%, and introduced a successful Supply Chain Financing solution to boost working capital. My tenure was marked by cross-functional collaboration, process automation, and actionable reporting that guided executive decisions. I also trained and mentored teams across multiple locations, improving reconciliation accuracy and operational discipline.

Earlier in my career, I gained a strong foundation in financial reporting, budgeting, and internal controls through roles as Financial Analyst and Accountant. These roles sharpened my ability to work hands-on with numbers while maintaining a strategic mindset—skills that continue to shape my leadership approach today.

I hold a Bachelor of Commerce in Finance, and CPA-K certification and I am a final year student for an MBA in Strategic Management.  I combine technical expertise with strong communication, negotiation, and leadership skills. I am passionate about continuous improvement, financial innovation, and building agile finance teams that thrive under pressure.

I’m always open to connecting with fellow professionals, thought leaders, and organizations driving financial transformation. Whether it's navigating complex funding structures, optimizing cash flows, or leading strategic treasury initiatives—I bring both the vision and execution required to deliver sustainable results.

Let’s connect.

author.headline: Senior Finance & Treasury Executive | Treasury & Liquidity Management | FX & Financial Risk Management | FP&A | Debt & Capital Strategy | Strategic Financial Transformation
author.about:
As a senior finance and treasury professional with over a decade of progressive experience, I have built my career around delivering strategic value through effective cash management, foreign exchange risk mitigation, and financial planning. My expertise lies in designing and executing treasury strategies that drive operational efficiency, ensure liquidity, reduce financial risk, and align closely with business goals.

Currently, I serve as Treasury Manager at Airtel Kenya, where I oversee multi-million-dollar FX operations, manage debt portfolios, and lead high-impact financial initiatives. One of my most notable achievements includes spearheading a $250 million de-dollarization project that reduced foreign currency exposure by 40% within a year—an initiative that earned me a fast-tracked promotion. I also developed and executed a full USD hedge policy that enhanced cash predictability and protected the business from currency volatility.

Previously, as Head of Treasury at Java House Group, I led company-wide treasury operations, significantly reduced bank charges by 80%, and introduced a successful Supply Chain Financing solution to boost working capital. My tenure was marked by cross-functional collaboration, process automation, and actionable reporting that guided executive decisions. I also trained and mentored teams across multiple locations, improving reconciliation accuracy and operational discipline.

Earlier in my career, I gained a strong foundation in financial reporting, budgeting, and internal controls through roles as Financial Analyst and Accountant. These roles sharpened my ability to work hands-on with numbers while maintaining a strategic mindset—skills that continue to shape my leadership approach today.

I hold a Bachelor of Commerce in Finance, and CPA-K certification and I am a final year student for an MBA in Strategic Management.  I combine technical expertise with strong communication, negotiation, and leadership skills. I am passionate about continuous improvement, financial innovation, and building agile finance teams that thrive under pressure.

I’m always open to connecting with fellow professionals, thought leaders, and organizations driving financial transformation. Whether it's navigating complex funding structures, optimizing cash flows, or leading strategic treasury initiatives—I bring both the vision and execution required to deliver sustainable results.

Let’s connect.

As Treasury Manager at Airtel Kenya Ltd, I lead strategic treasury operations in a fast-paced, high-stakes financial environment. I manage daily foreign exchange exposures exceeding USD 100 million and advise C-level leadership on effective hedging strategies to reduce currency volatility and enhance financial stability.

I streamline multi-entity cash forecasting processes, improving forecast accuracy by 35% and reducing idle cash holdings by 25%. I negotiate debt facilities totaling over KES 60billion, securing favorable interest terms while ensuring 100% compliance with loan covenants. My work directly supports the board by preparing macroeconomic reports that inform critical strategic decisions.

I oversee daily cash positioning, liquidity forecasting, and banking administration. I manage fixed deposit investments for optimal yield and counterparty compliance, and I coordinate bank reconciliations across more than 15 accounts—resolving discrepancies within 48 hours.

I ensure audit and regulatory compliance by maintaining documentation readiness and providing required financial insights. I also offer strategic input into capital allocation and cash optimization initiatives across the organization.

I take pride in mentoring and supervising a resilient, performance-driven treasury operations team. As Head of Treasury at Java House Group in Nairobi, I led the development and execution of the group-wide treasury strategy across East Africa. My focus was on optimizing liquidity, mitigating financial risk, and ensuring efficient capital utilization to support the company's growth objectives. I oversaw liquidity planning, FX risk management, debt structuring, and banking relationships while aligning treasury activities with corporate financial strategies.

I managed a debt portfolio exceeding KES 10 billion, ensuring full compliance with loan covenants and prudent financial governance. I consistently monitored KPIs, including bank charges, interest expenses, and liquidity ratios, to safeguard financial health. Through strategic renegotiation of banking terms, I successfully reduced bank charges by 80% and overdraft interest costs by 20%.

I was instrumental in the design and launch of a Supply Chain Financing solution that significantly improved our working capital position. I also led the integration of automated cash management tools with core finance systems to enhance transaction visibility and accuracy.

One of my key responsibilities involved preparing detailed weekly and monthly cash flow forecasts and conducting liquidity stress testing to prepare for market volatility. Additionally, I implemented a branch-level cash reconciliation training program, which resulted in a 60% reduction in reconciliation errors. I was honored to be named Employee of the Quarter (Q1 2020) for introducing impactful cost-saving innovations within the treasury function.

This role allowed me to work cross-functionally, training and supporting treasury teams across the region, building a strong control environment, and championing a culture of financial discipline and strategic foresight.

As a Financial Analyst at Java House Group, I supported strategic business decisions through data-driven insights and robust financial analysis. I was responsible for reviewing general ledger accounts, analyzing import costs, and evaluating intercompany transactions to ensure data accuracy and integrity across operations.

I developed and implemented dynamic financial models and cost-analysis tools that guided key business strategies and enhanced profitability. My role involved providing detailed analytical support during budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis, which helped improve forecast accuracy and align financial planning with company objectives.

One of my key contributions was standardizing monthly performance reports and executive dashboards, significantly improving visibility into critical KPIs for senior leadership. I played a pivotal role in month-end close processes, including reconciliations, accruals, and financial statement preparation, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.

Collaborating closely with procurement and supply chain teams, I assessed supplier pricing structures and identified cost-saving opportunities, contributing to margin improvement. I also supported internal control enhancements by identifying gaps in reporting processes and implementing corrective procedures that improved audit readiness.

Additionally, I assisted in internal audit preparation and compliance documentation while performing risk assessments and trend analyses to guide decisions on pricing and cost control. I produced ad hoc reports and scenario-based financial models to aid in tactical planning and investment decisions.

A notable achievement was improving gross margins by 10% through in-depth operational variance reviews. I also helped reduce reporting errors by 30% by automating manual processes and introducing validation checks. My performance led to a promotion within my first year in the role.

I maintained and analyzed general ledger accounts, ensured all transactions were accurately recorded, and complied with IFRS and internal accounting policies.

My responsibilities included overseeing petty cash management and reconciliation across all branches, conducting year-end cash counts, and reporting to head office finance. I led intercompany account reconciliations, resolving longstanding balances and improving financial alignment across subsidiaries. I was actively involved in the month-end and year-end close processes by preparing journal entries, accruals, and adjustments, which supported the delivery of timely and accurate financial statements.

I also facilitated both internal and external audit processes by preparing schedules, responding to audit queries, and ensuring accurate documentation. My role required me to perform daily and monthly bank reconciliations, investigate unmatched items, and maintain control over cash movements. I ensured full compliance with statutory obligations such as VAT, PAYE, and withholding tax, while maintaining accurate fixed asset registers and overseeing capital expenditure reporting. What if learning technology could lead to real-world experience and better career opportunities? 🚀

Meet Analytics Career Connect (ACC), a product-based EdTech, IT, and Recruitment Services startup headquartered in Pune, Maharashtra, India, founded by Mr. Wasim Patwari.

ACC is building an affordable and practical tech-learning ecosystem with a clear mission: to make technology education accessible, develop job-ready talent, and contribute to addressing unemployment in India—with an ambitious goal of helping 1 lakh job seekers secure employment. 🎯

💡 𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 → 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 → 𝗘𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗼𝘆𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆
We believe that learning becomes more meaningful when knowledge is applied in real-world situations. That is why ACC offers four digital products designed to support different career stages:

📊 1. Data Analyst Course with Internship Program
An affordable, structured learning pathway for beginners, combining technical fundamentals, hands-on practice, guided mentorship, and internship-style exposure.

💼 2. Placement Program
Practical projects, corporate-style tasks, mentorship, and placement support for learners who need more experience before entering the workforce.

📈 3. Job Assistance Program
Career support for experienced professionals through resume building, LinkedIn optimization, mock interviews, and referral-based job guidance, with a pay-after-hiring model.

🎓 4. Campus to Corporate (C2C)
A practical pathway for college students to develop industry-relevant skills, confidence, and business problem-solving experience before starting their careers.

🌱 Beyond our products, ACC embraces a startup culture built on ownership, growth, initiative, and learning by doing. We value individuals who are curious, proactive, and ready to contribute, not just observe.
At ACC, we aim to connect knowledge with action and potential with opportunity.💡
Analytics Career Connect

author.about:
At Analytics Career Connect, we are committed to addressing two of India’s biggest challenges: Employment and Affordable Education.
Vision: To make education and career opportunities affordable, accessible, and effective for every learner and job seeker in India.
Goal: To support 1 lakh job seekers in securing meaningful employment and help students gain industry-ready skills through structured training and mentorship.
ACC is a growing ecosystem combining EdTech, HR services, and placement programs, designed to bridge the gap between talent and opportunity. Our approach integrates learning, practical exposure, and analytics-driven hiring solutions.

What We Offer:
 1️⃣ Data & IT Domain Mentorship + Internship +  Training
 2️⃣ Data & IT Placement & Job Assistance Programs
 3️⃣ HR Internship, Mentorship & Training Program
 4️⃣ Industry-readiness programs for Job Seekers and Students.

If you are looking for internships, mentorship, training, or job opportunities in HR, Marketing, Data, IT, Graphic Design, or other domains we are here to support you.
  📩 Connect for opportunities:
  🌐 Company Page : https://analyticscareerconnect.com
  📧 hr@analyticscareerconnect.com
  📬 For Quick Reply : harimu.hr.acc@gmail.com





Master’s degree holder in Educational Management from Universitas Negeri Malang, with a BNSP-certified Human Resources Staff qualification and experience across human resources administration, healthcare services, education, and organizational development. Experienced in supporting HR and talent development initiatives, including mentoring and developing 15+ participants, conducting Training Needs Analysis (TNA) and Talent Mapping for 28 members, and coordinating organizational programs involving 30+ committee members. Skilled in HR administration, program planning and implementation, competency development, employee/member engagement, and cross-functional coordination. Demonstrated leadership experience in planning and coordinating 15 organizational programs, with a strong interest in human capital development and building effective, collaborative teams.

🔐 Job Opportunity: Network Security Engineer

We are looking for skilled Network Security Engineers with hands-on experience in network firewalls and cybersecurity/SOC operations to join a reputed organization in Bangalore.

✅ Key Skills & Responsibilities:

• Hands-on experience with any Network Firewall technology – Palo Alto, Fortinet, Cisco, Check Point, or equivalent
• Strong knowledge of Firewall Configuration, Policy Management, and Troubleshooting
• Experience in Network Security Monitoring and Threat Detection
• Knowledge of SOC Operations, Security Incident Management, and Incident Response
• Understanding of SIEM tools such as Splunk, IBM QRadar, or Microsoft Sentinel
• Knowledge of VPN, IDS/IPS, Network Traffic Analysis, and Access Control
• Experience in Security Event Analysis, Log Monitoring, and Threat Investigation

posts.content:
A Walk-In Interview Shouldn’t Mean Walking Into Disappointment.

Recently, a friend of mine attended a walk-in interview at Stantec, hoping for a fair opportunity to showcase her skills and explore a new career opportunity. Unfortunately, what she experienced was far from a professional candidate experience.

She reached the venue at around 11:00 AM and patiently waited for over 2 hours just for the first round of interviews.

When she was finally called in, she was informed that her resume had reached the interview panel only 5 minutes before the discussion.

After a brief initial conversation, she was told that the team would get back to her in case there were any further rounds in the coming week.

What made the experience even more disappointing was that the conversation gave a strong impression that the position might already have been closed.

This raises some genuine concerns about how walk-in interviews are being managed.

A few questions worth asking:

🔹 Why should candidates wait for hours when their resumes haven’t even reached the interview panel?

🔹 Who is accountable for managing the interview schedule and ensuring candidates’ time is respected?

🔹 If there is no immediate hiring requirement, why not communicate that transparently instead of leaving candidates with uncertainty?

Let’s remember something important: A candidate’s time is just as valuable as a company’s time.

Candidates take time off work, manage personal commitments, travel to the venue, and invest their energy and expectations in these opportunities. They show up prepared, hopeful, and ready to give their best.

The least they deserve in return is an organised process, clear communication, and basic professional courtesy.

Recruitment is not just about evaluating candidates. It is also about the experience organisations create for them. Every interaction contributes to an employer’s reputation, whether the candidate gets selected or not.

A rejection is understandable. Delays can happen. Hiring requirements can change. But poor coordination and a lack of transparency should not become part of the candidate experience.

Companies invest significantly in employer branding, but employer branding begins with how candidates are treated on the ground.

I hope organisations take this as a reminder to make their hiring processes more structured, transparent, and respectful of candidates’ time.

Because candidates are not just resumes in a queue. They are professionals deserving of respect.

#CandidateExperience #Recruitment #HiringProcess #EmployerBranding #HR #TalentAcquisition

posts.content:
In 1991, a 21-year-old student in Helsinki posted a message that changed the world.
Linus Torvalds wasn't trying to disrupt an industry. He was a university student who wanted a Unix-like operating system that ran on his own PC. Commercial Unix was expensive, and the alternatives weren't quite what he wanted.
So he started building one.
In August 1991 he posted to a Usenet group, saying it was "just a hobby" and wouldn't be big or professional. A few weeks later, Linux 0.01 was out: roughly ten thousand lines of code.
The decision that changed everything
In 1992, Linus released Linux under the GNU General Public License. Anyone could use it, study it, modify it, and share it, as long as they shared their improvements back.
Developers around the world started contributing. The kernel grew through thousands of small improvements from people who had never met.
The ecosystem it created
Red Hat (1993) proved you could build a billion-dollar business on open source. IBM acquired it in 2019 for $34B.
SUSE and Canonical (Ubuntu) built enterprise and desktop distributions.
Android runs on the Linux kernel, putting it in billions of pockets.
AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud run most of their workloads on Linux.
Docker and Kubernetes exist because of Linux kernel features like namespaces and cgroups.
The Linux Foundation now coordinates open-source work across the industry.

rawPayload.content:
In 1991, a 21-year-old student in Helsinki posted a message that changed the world.
Linus Torvalds wasn't trying to disrupt an industry. He was a university student who wanted a Unix-like operating system that ran on his own PC. Commercial Unix was expensive, and the alternatives weren't quite what he wanted.
So he started building one.
In August 1991 he posted to a Usenet group, saying it was "just a hobby" and wouldn't be big or professional. A few weeks later, Linux 0.01 was out: roughly ten thousand lines of code.
The decision that changed everything
In 1992, Linus released Linux under the GNU General Public License. Anyone could use it, study it, modify it, and share it, as long as they shared their improvements back.
Developers around the world started contributing. The kernel grew through thousands of small improvements from people who had never met.
The ecosystem it created
Red Hat (1993) proved you could build a billion-dollar business on open source. IBM acquired it in 2019 for $34B.
SUSE and Canonical (Ubuntu) built enterprise and desktop distributions.
Android runs on the Linux kernel, putting it in billions of pockets.
AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud run most of their workloads on Linux.
Docker and Kubernetes exist because of Linux kernel features like namespaces and cgroups.
The Linux Foundation now coordinates open-source work across the industry.
Every one of the world's top 500 supercomputers runs Linux.

Big things often start as small, personal itches.

What does it mean for the past to be fixed, and for the future to remain open?
Physics can orient the arrow of time. It is less often asked what gives a moment the status of a record.
In my monograph, Records, Irreversibility, and the Arrow of Time, I separate two questions that are usually treated as one:
Direction — why Entropy or complexity increases toward one side of the time axis
Status — what makes part of history fixed, while the rest remains open
The standard package answers the first through a low-entropy origin. 
The second is then treated as a corollary. I argue that this is too quick.

Within Informational Monism, temporal asymmetry is not one master fact. It is a family of related operations:
local irreversible commitment of records
complexity-resolved loss of accessibility
and a cosmic constraint against terminal saturation

A record is not merely a correlation. It is a pointer alternative anchored by dissipation. 
Once stabilized, it is undone only at an exponentially suppressed probability. 
From this, a partial order of records can be defined without requiring a global foliation of spacetime.

This monograph completes a four-part foundational sequence:
Black Hole Information — what remains available
Quantum Measurement — what becomes actual
Bell Correlations — what remains of separability
The Arrow of Time — what is fixed, and what remains open

The work does not derive the thermodynamic arrow, replace statistical mechanics, or claim a final cosmology. It offers something more limited and more precise: a clearer architecture for the difference between a world that merely evolves and a world in which something can be said to have happened.

posts.content:
Should private companies be able to use Nepal's national grid to sell electricity directly, and at what price?

On 1 October, the Electricity Regulatory Commission issued Nepal's first standard for calculating transmission "wheeling charges", the fee for using the national grid. For short-term open access, it set the charge at 57 paisa per unit (kWh). This opens the grid to private power traders for the first time. The Independent Power Producers' Association, Nepal (IPPAN) welcomed the move but says the rates are too high for domestic and cross-border trade.

Both sides have a serious case.

The case for higher charges: The grid was built largely with public money and loans. If private traders pay too little, the cost of maintaining and expanding it falls on Nepal Electricity Authority and, in the end, on ordinary consumers.

The case for lower charges: Open access only works if trading is viable. High fees could keep private buyers and sellers out, leaving surplus wet-season power unsold while industries still face supply gaps. Lower charges could also help Nepal export more to India and Bangladesh.

The deeper question is what the grid is for: a cost-recovery asset for the state utility, or a public platform that should grow the whole power market.

Where do you stand: protect NEA's finances, keep charges low to grow private trade, or phase rates down over time?

rawPayload.content:
Should private companies be able to use Nepal's national grid to sell electricity directly, and at what price?

On 1 October, the Electricity Regulatory Commission issued Nepal's first standard for calculating transmission "wheeling charges", the fee for using the national grid. For short-term open access, it set the charge at 57 paisa per unit (kWh). This opens the grid to private power traders for the first time. The Independent Power Producers' Association, Nepal (IPPAN) welcomed the move but says the rates are too high for domestic and cross-border trade.

Both sides have a serious case.

The case for higher charges: The grid was built largely with public money and loans. If private traders pay too little, the cost of maintaining and expanding it falls on Nepal Electricity Authority and, in the end, on ordinary consumers.

The case for lower charges: Open access only works if trading is viable. High fees could keep private buyers and sellers out, leaving surplus wet-season power unsold while industries still face supply gaps. Lower charges could also help Nepal export more to India and Bangladesh.

The deeper question is what the grid is for: a cost-recovery asset for the state utility, or a public platform that should grow the whole power market.

Where do you stand: protect NEA's finances, keep charges low to grow private trade, or phase rates down over time?


#EnergyPolicy #Nepal #Hydropower #PowerTrade #PolicyPulseNepal

Signs Your Garage Door Needs Repair
October 10, 2026


Your garage door gets used every day. Changes in its sound or movement can be a sign that it needs attention. Here are five signs to watch for.

New or unusual noises

Grinding, scraping, or loud banging can point to worn or damaged parts. Have new noises checked instead of repeatedly running the door.

Jerking or uneven movement

A door that shakes, sticks, or moves crookedly needs an inspection. If it looks off track, stop using it and keep people clear.

Trouble opening or closing

If the door stops partway or reverses unexpectedly, several issues could be involved, including the opener or safety sensors. Don’t bypass the safety sensors or force the door.

Visible damage

Frayed cables, bent tracks, damaged rollers, or a visible gap in a spring are reasons to call a garage door professional. Springs and cables are under tension—leave those repairs to a trained technician.

Changes in how the opener works

If the motor runs but the door barely moves, or operation becomes unreliable, have the door and opener checked together before assuming the opener needs replacement.

posts.content:
A common situation in maintenance teams: a component fails, the team pays for the repair, and weeks later someone finds out it was still under warranty.

It isn't negligence. Warranty dates sit in purchase files, contracts sit with procurement, and the maintenance team only sees the broken equipment in front of them.

In NextEAM, warranties and service contracts sit on the asset record itself. Procurement runs on a three-way match between purchase order, receipt and invoice. So when a technician opens a work order, they can see right away whether the vendor should be covering the cost.

Small details like this decide whether an asset management system pays for itself.

Does your maintenance team see warranty status when it opens a work order?

#NextEAM #Procurement #SupplyChain #ContractManagement #WarrantyManagement #MaintenanceManagement #EnterpriseAssetManagement #CostOptimization #Operations #SaudiArabia #GCC #DigitalTransformation

posts.content:
🙏 Inspired by a thoughtful discussion with Hamed Latifi Shafie, Senior Machinery & PMV Manager, on managing deferred defects in heavy equipment.


🔧 CONTROLLED DEFERRAL vs. FORGOTTEN DEFERRAL
Not every unresolved defect requires an immediate shutdown.
But every decision to keep operating must rest on technical evidence, not convenience.
A deferred defect is acceptable only when it is a managed risk, not just an open work order.
1️⃣ VERIFY BEFORE YOU DECIDE
A low oil-pressure indication could be a gauge fault or real lubrication starvation. The right decision differs in each case.
→ Verify the condition independently first.
2️⃣ SET STOP CRITERIA BEFORE THE DECISION
Not at 2 a.m. under production pressure.
Examples: a confirmed value below a set limit, a rising trend, abnormal noise or temperature.
→ If the severe failure mode cannot be ruled out, availability does not justify running.
3️⃣ STANDARDIZE THE PROCESS, NOT EVERY THRESHOLD
Fleet-wide process:
Report → Assess risk → Authorize → Monitor → Close
Machine-specific limits:
Based on OEM specifications, the system involved and the failure mode.
One engine model's oil-pressure limit cannot be applied to another.
4️⃣ TREAT LIMITS AS CONTROLLED DATA
Clear source. Revision history. Linked to the defect record.
Review them when conditions, components, OEM requirements or failure history change, and periodically to confirm they are still current.
A relevant change triggers reassessment immediately, not at the next scheduled review.
📋 WHAT EVERY DEFERRED RECORD NEEDS
- Reason for deferral
- Operating restrictions and interim controls
- Stop criteria
- Monitoring frequency
- Responsible owner
- Closure deadline
- Date of last review
⚠️ WHY DEFERRALS STAY OPEN
Parts delays and operating pressure can both extend a deferral.
Which is more common? Only the defect history and closure data can tell you.
The real question is:
Is this deferral technically controlled…
or is it open simply because nobody followed up?
📊 A SIMPLE INDICATOR
Days since last review, on every deferred record.
No activity = a follow-up gap. A follow-up gap becomes exposure.
🎯 KEY TAKEAWAY
Deferral is not the problem. Uncontrolled deferral is.
Evidence → Controls → Owner → Review → Closure
💬 Question for maintenance professionals:
Do you set a maximum time between reviews of open deferrals based on criticality?
#MaintenanceManagement #ReliabilityEngineering #AssetManagement #RiskManagement #DeferredMaintenance #HeavyEquipment #MaintenancePlanning
— Mustafa Zaki

posts.content:
**RISK-WEIGHTED BACKLOG: NOT ALL WORK ORDERS ARE EQUAL**
*100 open work orders do not necessarily represent more risk than 10.*
Imagine two manufacturing plants.
🏭 **Plant A**
* 120 deferred work orders
* Most involve low-consequence defects
* Critical tasks are controlled and monitored
🏭 **Plant B**
* Only 25 deferred work orders
* Several involve critical rotating equipment
* One known defect could trigger a major production interruption
Which plant has the greater maintenance risk?
**The work-order count alone cannot tell you.**
This is why maintenance organizations should move beyond counting deferred tasks and start evaluating their associated risk.
### 1️⃣ Start with the failure mode
For each deferred work order, ask:
* What can fail?
* What is the credible failure mechanism?
* How likely is the failure under current operating conditions?
* What are the consequences?
* What controls are currently in place?
Asset criticality is useful, but it does not replace a task-specific assessment of the failure mode and its consequences.
### 2️⃣ Apply a consistent risk method
A simple screening method may use:
**Risk Score = Likelihood Rating × Consequence Rating**
Example using a hypothetical 5 × 5 matrix:
* Likelihood = 4
* Consequence = 5
* Risk score = 4 × 5 = **20**
This indicates a high-priority exposure if the site's approved matrix classifies 20 that way.
However, not every risk matrix uses simple multiplication, and equal numerical scores may represent different risk profiles. Follow your site's approved methodology.
### 3️⃣ Calculate a risk-weighted backlog indicator
One possible management indicator is:
**Risk-Weighted Backlog Index (%)**
= Current aggregate deferred-risk score ÷ Baseline aggregate deferred-risk score × 100
Example:
Baseline aggregate score = 400
Current aggregate score = 520
Index = 520 ÷ 400 × 100 = **130%**
The aggregate score is 30% higher than the baseline.
That is a reason to investigate—not proof that the plant's actual failure probability has increased by 30%.

rawPayload.content:
**RISK-WEIGHTED BACKLOG: NOT ALL WORK ORDERS ARE EQUAL**
*100 open work orders do not necessarily represent more risk than 10.*
Imagine two manufacturing plants.
🏭 **Plant A**
* 120 deferred work orders
* Most involve low-consequence defects
* Critical tasks are controlled and monitored
🏭 **Plant B**
* Only 25 deferred work orders
* Several involve critical rotating equipment
* One known defect could trigger a major production interruption
Which plant has the greater maintenance risk?
**The work-order count alone cannot tell you.**
This is why maintenance organizations should move beyond counting deferred tasks and start evaluating their associated risk.
### 1️⃣ Start with the failure mode
For each deferred work order, ask:
* What can fail?
* What is the credible failure mechanism?
* How likely is the failure under current operating conditions?
* What are the consequences?
* What controls are currently in place?
Asset criticality is useful, but it does not replace a task-specific assessment of the failure mode and its consequences.
### 2️⃣ Apply a consistent risk method
A simple screening method may use:
**Risk Score = Likelihood Rating × Consequence Rating**
Example using a hypothetical 5 × 5 matrix:
* Likelihood = 4
* Consequence = 5
* Risk score = 4 × 5 = **20**
This indicates a high-priority exposure if the site's approved matrix classifies 20 that way.
However, not every risk matrix uses simple multiplication, and equal numerical scores may represent different risk profiles. Follow your site's approved methodology.
### 3️⃣ Calculate a risk-weighted backlog indicator
One possible management indicator is:
**Risk-Weighted Backlog Index (%)**
= Current aggregate deferred-risk score ÷ Baseline aggregate deferred-risk score × 100
Example:
Baseline aggregate score = 400
Current aggregate score = 520
Index = 520 ÷ 400 × 100 = **130%**
The aggregate score is 30% higher than the baseline.
That is a reason to investigate—not proof that the plant's actual failure probability has increased by 30%.
For meaningful comparisons, use a consistent risk matrix, scoring rules, asset scope, and reporting period. Define how completed work, new deferrals, repeat deferrals, and changes in operating conditions affect the index.
### 4️⃣ Never let the total hide a critical task
An aggregate indicator can conceal a single unacceptable exposure.

#ReliabilityEngineering #MaintenanceManagement #RiskBasedMaintenance #AssetManagement #MaintenancePlanning #RiskManagement #OperationalExcellence

posts.content:
Project spending to date does not tell you what finishing will cost.
A useful cost-to-complete review starts with the remaining work, then connects it to the resources and commitments required to deliver it.
Check four distinct elements:
• Actual costs already recorded.
• Costs incurred but not yet recorded.
• Open commitments for work still to be delivered.
• Remaining work without a purchase order or other commitment.
Keep incurred costs separate from future costs, and avoid counting an amount in more than one category.
Illustrative example: an open purchase order may include work already completed and accrued. Adding the full order value to the accrual would overstate the forecast.
Ask the delivery owner to validate quantities, timing and unresolved scope changes. Finance can test the calculation, but the estimate needs operational evidence.
Keep the latest estimate alongside the approved baseline, with a clear explanation of what changed.
#ProjectFinance #CostControl

My background covers P&L management, forecasting, capital allocation, working capital and financial reporting. These areas come together when evaluating a commercial proposal, reviewing performance, planning cash requirements or improving how management receives information.
The questions that shape this work are practical. What assumptions support the plan? What changes the margin or cash requirement? Who owns the response when performance moves away from expectations?

currentPosition.description:
Placement Executive 

Career Objective

A dedicated and result-oriented Placement Executive with experience in candidate placement, employer engagement, and placement operations under skill development programs. Skilled in building corporate relationships, coordinating recruitment drives, ensuring successful candidate placements, and maintaining compliance with organizational and project guidelines.

Key Responsibilities

- Develop and maintain relationships with employers and corporate partners.
- Identify job opportunities suitable for trained candidates.
- Organize placement drives, campus interviews, and job fairs.
- Coordinate interviews between employers and candidates.
- Prepare candidates through resume building, interview guidance, and soft skills support.
- Ensure timely joining of selected candidates.
- Track post-placement retention and conduct regular follow-ups with candidates and employers.
- Maintain placement records, documentation, MIS reports, and compliance as per DDU-GKY SOP.
- Achieve placement targets and support overall project objectives.
- Work closely with training, mobilization, and project teams to ensure successful placement outcomes.

Key Skills

- Corporate Relations
- Placement Coordination
- Recruitment Support
- Candidate Counselling
- Employer Engagement
- Interview Coordination
- Documentation & Compliance
- MIS Reporting (MS Excel, Word)
- Communication & Negotiation
- Teamwork and Time Management

author.headline: Founder at Hireoptix
author.about:
Building HireOptix — a skill-first hiring platform for India’s optical and eye care industry.

Hiring in this space is still largely CV-driven, while actual performance depends on clinical decision-making, product understanding, and communication. HireOptix focuses on solving this gap by enabling employers to evaluate candidates based on real-world scenarios before hiring.

The platform combines structured assessments, practical simulations, and candidate profiles to make hiring faster, more reliable, and outcome-driven.

Currently working towards creating a standardized “HireOptix Score” that can become a trusted benchmark for optometrists across the industry.

Exploring how data, skill validation, and real-world performance signals can reshape hiring in frontline healthcare roles.

author.headline: Founder at Hireoptix
author.about:
Building HireOptix — a skill-first hiring platform for India’s optical and eye care industry.

Hiring in this space is still largely CV-driven, while actual performance depends on clinical decision-making, product understanding, and communication. HireOptix focuses on solving this gap by enabling employers to evaluate candidates based on real-world scenarios before hiring.

The platform combines structured assessments, practical simulations, and candidate profiles to make hiring faster, more reliable, and outcome-driven.

Currently working towards creating a standardized “HireOptix Score” that can become a trusted benchmark for optometrists across the industry.

Exploring how data, skill validation, and real-world performance signals can reshape hiring in frontline healthcare roles.

Working on improving hiring in the optical industry by shifting focus from CVs to real skills.

posts.content:
FOLLOW Vishvesh Birajdar FOR SUCH A MORE POSTS.

🚀 November to February: Is This the Best Time to Switch Jobs?
For experienced IT professionals, one question comes up every year:
👉 “When should I start looking for a new job?
”If you’re planning a switch in the next few months, 
the November–February period can be an important window.
Here’s how I would approach it 👇
📅 NOVEMBER — START
Don’t wait until January.
✅ Update your resume
✅ Optimize LinkedIn
✅ Identify target companies
✅ Start networking
✅ Contact recruiters
✅ Begin applying
✅ Start interview preparation
If you want to switch in January/February, November is the time to start.🎄

author.about:
Deuchar is an internationally renowned Criminologist, and experienced leader and manager in Higher Education. He is a Professor of Criminology and former Fulbright Scholar with a demonstrated history of working in the Higher Education industry in the U.K. and USA. He is a strong education professional with a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) from University of Strathclyde.

Deuchar is the author of several highly acclaimed Criminology books: his 2009 work 'Gangs, Marginalised Youth and Social Capital' (Trentham Books) is the most widely cited modern academic book on gangs in Scotland. Its sequel, 'Policing Youth Violence: Transatlantic Connections' (2013, IOE Press) is the only published piece of work to include a comparative study on how focused deterrence was used to reduce gang violence in both Cincinnati, Ohio and Glasgow, Scotland. His third criminology text, 'Young People and Social Control' (Palgrave macMillan) was launched in September 2017, co-authored with Prof Kalwant Bhopal, and provides a multi-perspective analysis of how agents of control operate in the lives of disadvantaged young people. His most recent book, ‘Gangs and Spirituality’ (Palgrave MacMillan) was release in summer 2018 and examines the role of religion and spirituality (including meditation) in desistance from crime and disengagement from gangs from a global perspective. 

Deuchar is in high demand as a keynote speaker and after dinner speaker, where he regularly shares his unique research insights into gangs, gang intervention programmes, spirituality and policing. If interested in inviting him to speak at an event please visit: https://www.rossdeuchar.me.uk/contact

Deuchar was a Fulbright Scholar-in-Residence in the School of Criminology and Criminal Justice at Florida Atlantic University (FAU), USA, during the 2016/17 spring semester. He was appointed as Affiliate Professor of Criminology at FAU in April 2017. For further information on his academic work please visit: https://rossdeuchar.me.uk or follow Professor Deuchar on Twitter: @rossdeuchar

Deuchar is also a fully qualified Personal Trainer and a certified Life Coach & Meditation teacher. For further information on this please follow Deuchar on Twitter: @deuchar_ross or email: johngrady@gmail.com

posts.content:
I’ve written enough cover letters to know that introducing yourself to the world is not as easy as it sounds.

Since I started job hunting, I’ve written cover letters, crafted cold emails, researched brands, reached out to professionals, and applied for opportunities across PR, communications, media, and entertainment.

I’ve tried to make every application intentional, connecting what an organisation does with what I can contribute and what I’m eager to learn.

Some applications have ended in rejection. Others have received no response at all.

Honestly, it can be exhausting.

There’s a particular vulnerability in repeatedly introducing yourself to people who may never know you beyond a CV or a carefully written email. You research, find the right words, press send, and hope someone sees enough potential to respond.

Sometimes they do. Sometimes they don’t.

But this journey is teaching me more than how to apply for jobs. It’s teaching me how to communicate my value, research before reaching out, and articulate what I bring to the table, even while I’m still discovering the full extent of my abilities.

Funny enough, while seeking opportunities to practise communication professionally, I’ve had to practise it just to get those opportunities.

I know enthusiasm alone cannot replace experience, and there’s still so much I need to learn. But being at the beginning of my career doesn’t mean I have nothing to offer.

I have ideas, curiosity, and a willingness to learn, contribute, and grow.

So, I am still writing, researching, applying, and reaching out. Not because every attempt has worked, but because I refuse to let unsuccessful attempts define my potential.

To every recruiter and professional who takes the time to respond to an applicant, offer feedback, or give emerging talent a chance: your response may mean more than you realise.

For now, I’m still learning, still showing up, and still putting myself out there.

One application at a time.

#CareerJourney #PublicRelations #Communications #JobSearch

author.about:
Steven Cummings has been drawing and inking comic books for well over 20 years.  His work includes both interior sequential page illustration as well as cover art composition and art.  https://www.artstation.com/sutesuke

He has worked most recently for Marvel Comics on Star Wars related comic books as well as Fantastic Four.  Other notable comic book publishers include DC Comics and Udon Entertainment and he also draws for Role Playing Game publishers most notably Palladium Books.  

He spent several years drawing the creator owned comic book Wayward published by Image Comics.

Steven is skilled at layout and both the drawing and the inking of comic book pages and is comfortable working with creative teams in book creation.
He also is fluent in Japanese and has worked in translation and interpretation roles.

🚀 Web for Google Messages — New release v7.0!

v7.0 - 10/10/2026
✨ NEW modern look: rounded side menu, menus, messages and mini tutorial, cleaner top-bar buttons in the same places and sizes, the same on every site

🌙 NEW Dark Mode in the side menu: AUTO (like your computer), ON or OFF

🌑 NEW Dark skin: makes light pages dark and leaves dark pages as they are

📐 NEW top-bar button: the window goes back to its default size and position in one click

🛟 Safer window: if a monitor is unplugged or the place doesn’t fit, the window opens on the main screen instead of not opening

🎥 NEW Video of the window: 5, 15 or 30 seconds, your own time, or start and stop yourself (saved as MP4)

🎓 The mini tutorial now shows every option: the side menu (Theme – Skin Color, Multi Window – Account, Incognito, Changelog…) and the new buttons, without scrolling the page

🔄 Edge: after an update or a restart, the open window shows “click here to reload”, so the top bar keeps working

👥 NEW “New Window & Account”: open a second window with another account, side by side (allow the extension in private windows: “Allow in InPrivate” on Edge, “Run in Private Windows” on Firefox)

🦊 Firefox: NEW “New Window” too, a second window of the same account

🪟 New Window opens a little to the side, so you see both windows

🎨 Theme – Skin Color reworked: the skin covers the whole site while the top bar and menus keep their colours, “None” really clears it and “Invert” is now a real dark mode 🌙

📱 New phone pairing help with today’s steps (Device pairing › Google Account pairing › tap the matching emoji), also in the side menu

💬 Google Chat: the conversation and the message box are no longer cut at the bottom

🎥 Meet: the header and the “Enter a code / Join” box sit right under the top bar

🎥 Meet: in a call, the time, the meeting code and the people show under the top bar, and the call buttons stay in the window

🐞 The Messages / Meet / Chat switcher menu opens right under its button

🐞 Google Chat and Meet: Theme – Skin Color, Multi Window and the other side-menu options work again

🕶️ Incognito mode works again on Google Chat and now also on Meet

🔗 Right-click › “Open in Web for Google Messages” now also on Meet and Google Chat links

🐞 Round of Bugfixes: the top bar shows on the first open, SideBar/WideBar work at the first click after you resize the window, Screenshot always takes the extension window

🖼️ News & Tips: pictures load on every site and the messages show at most once a day

🎓 Mini tutorial and popup buttons look right on every site

📐 Top bar: the menu button sits in line with the other buttons on every site, and nothing under the bar blocks clicks on the page

🔒 Security improvements and no more warnings on the extension’s Errors page

#WebForGoogleMessages #Messaging #Update

posts.content:
A JOURNEY OF GROWTH, COURAGE, AND GRATITUDE ALHAMDULILLAH 🤲🎓

Yesterday, I received an email informing me that I was not selected for the 2026/2027 Click On Kaduna Data Science Fellowship Programme (DSFP 6.0).

Although the news was disappointing, I choose to focus on the progress, experience, and lessons gained throughout the journey.

This was my first attempt at the DSFP, and I am grateful to have progressed through the application process, assessment, and interview stages to become one of the final candidates considered for the available 40 slots.

According to the programme team, approximately 182 outstanding applicants reached the interview stage, competing for just 40 available places. Being part of that final stage was an achievement I will always appreciate.

As a Statistics graduate from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, with a growing passion for Data Science, Data Analytics, and Machine Learning, this experience has strengthened my determination to keep learning, building practical projects, and seeking opportunities to apply data to real-world problems.

I may not have secured a place in this cohort, but I have gained experience, confidence, and a clearer vision of where I am going.

I sincerely appreciate the DSFP 6.0 team for the opportunity to participate in this competitive selection process.

To everyone who supported, encouraged, and prayed for me throughout this journey, thank you. Your support means a lot.

I believe that Allah’s plans are always best. I will keep working, improving my skills, and trusting His timing.

This is not the end of the journey; it is another opportunity to grow, prepare, and come back stronger. 💪

Alhamdulillah for the opportunity, the lessons, and the journey. 🤲

#DataScience #DataAnalytics #MachineLearning #ContinuousLearning #CareerGrowth #ClickOnKaduna #DSFP60

1. Play a leading role in the development of Australia’s resources via the promotion of Australian industry, including SME participation, in international markets.

3. Make representations to and on behalf of exporters to appropriate decision makers

4. Undertake research to identify and quantify the issues affecting the development of profitable international trade activity by Australian SME companies. 

5. Interface with and provide support to sector specific associations and councils representing business engaged in international trade. 

6. Deliver activities which: Provide a forum for the exchange of ideas and knowledge & Reward excellence in export.

posts.content:
A cold-room alarm nobody sees is just a log entry.

That's why this week's update to FactoraERP IoT matters to me: plant-floor alerts now go out by SMS and WhatsApp, as well as email.

Here's how it works. Gateways and sensors from hardware partners such as Teltonika and Milesight stream temperature, energy and vibration readings into FactoraERP. When a reading drifts, the alert goes to a named person, and their acknowledgement is recorded. The same alarm can open a maintenance work order.

Because the monitoring lives inside the ERP, every reading is tied to the batch in that cold room. So when a buyer or auditor asks what happened last night, the answer is already on record, and the temperature audit trail exports in one click.

We also designed it for real plant conditions. Gateways buffer readings when the network drops and sync when it comes back.

The SMS and WhatsApp alerts run on the Africa's Talking messaging API.

We're now looking for our first pilot factories: food and agro-processors, cold stores and manufacturers who want monitoring that turns into action. Pricing on request.

More at factoraiot.com

#FactoraERP #IndustrialIoT #Manufacturing #FoodSafety #ColdChain #SmartFactory

posts.content:
A cold-room alarm nobody sees is just a log entry.

That's why this week's update to FactoraERP IoT matters to me: plant-floor alerts now go out by SMS and WhatsApp, as well as email.

Here's how it works. Gateways and sensors from hardware partners such as Teltonika and Milesight stream temperature, energy and vibration readings into FactoraERP. When a reading drifts, the alert goes to a named person, and their acknowledgement is recorded. The same alarm can open a maintenance work order.

Because the monitoring lives inside the ERP, every reading is tied to the batch in that cold room. So when a buyer or auditor asks what happened last night, the answer is already on record, and the temperature audit trail exports in one click.

We also designed it for real plant conditions. Gateways buffer readings when the network drops and sync when it comes back.

The SMS and WhatsApp alerts run on the Africa's Talking messaging API.

We're now looking for our first pilot factories: food and agro-processors, cold stores and manufacturers who want monitoring that turns into action. Pricing on request.

More at factoraiot.com

posts.content:
Your content might be getting views. But is it bringing you opportunities?

Let's reflect on what this week taught us about building a strong digital presence.

Because being online is one thing.

Being visible, trusted, and chosen is another.

Here are 5 lessons worth carrying into next week. 👇

1. Visibility without strategy is wasted potential.

Posting every day isn't enough.

Your content needs to communicate your value, attract the right audience, and give people a reason to work with you.

2. Your positioning determines how people perceive you.

Can someone visit your LinkedIn profile and immediately understand what you do, who you help, and why they should choose you?

If not, you may be losing opportunities before the conversation even begins.

3. Your personal brand should build trust.

People want to understand your expertise before they hire you.

Share your knowledge. Demonstrate your skills. Address real problems.

Don't just tell people you're good at what you do. Show them.

4. Your LinkedIn profile should do more than list your experience.

It should communicate your value, highlight your strengths, and help the right people see you as a credible professional.

Your profile is part of your first impression. Make it count.

5. Your digital presence should support your business goals.

Whether you're a professional seeking opportunities or a business looking for customers, your online presence needs direction.

Every post, profile section, and platform should serve a purpose.

Now, let's talk about YOUR digital presence.

If you're struggling to communicate your value online, attract the right audience, or turn your social media activity into meaningful opportunities, I can help.

Here's how we can work together:

🔹 LinkedIn Profile Optimization — Position your profile to communicate your expertise, strengths, and professional value.

🔹 Personal Branding Strategy — Build a clear, consistent brand that helps you stand out in your industry.

🔹 Social Media Management — Get strategic content planning and management that keeps your brand visible and relevant.

🔹 Content Strategy — Develop purposeful content that educates your audience, demonstrates your expertise, and supports your business goals.

🔹 CV & Cover Letter Writing — Present your experience and qualifications professionally with tailored, ATS-conscious application documents.

I don't believe in posting just to stay active.

I believe in building a digital presence with purpose.

Be Seen. Be Chosen.

📩 Ready to work together?

Send me a DM on LinkedIn or reach out directly:

📱 WhatsApp: +254 723 298768

📧 Email: chantal@tsnexperience.com

Let's make your digital presence work harder for you.

One question before you scroll:

Is your online presence communicating your value, or are people still guessing what you do?

posts.content:
A cold-room alarm nobody sees is just a log entry.

That's why this week's update to FactoraERP IoT matters to me: plant-floor alerts now go out by SMS and WhatsApp, as well as email.

Here's how it works. Gateways and sensors from hardware partners such as Teltonika and Milesight stream temperature, energy and vibration readings into FactoraERP. When a reading drifts, the alert goes to a named person, and their acknowledgement is recorded. The same alarm can open a maintenance work order.

Because the monitoring lives inside the ERP, every reading is tied to the batch in that cold room. So when a buyer or auditor asks what happened last night, the answer is already on record, and the temperature audit trail exports in one click.

We also designed it for real plant conditions. Gateways buffer readings when the network drops and sync when it comes back.

The SMS and WhatsApp alerts run on the Africa's Talking messaging API.

We're now looking for our first pilot factories: food and agro-processors, cold stores and manufacturers who want monitoring that turns into action. Pricing on request.

More at factoraiot.com

#FactoraERP #IndustrialIoT #Manufacturing #FoodSafety #ColdChain #SmartFactory

author.about:
I'm Isaac Mwendwa Muthui, Founder & CTO of Tamalaki Business Network, a Nairobi-based innovation holding company that designs, owns and operates AI-native platforms across agriculture, manufacturing, construction, exports and smart infrastructure.

At Tamalaki, I've founded or co-founded a connected set of ventures, each serving one part of the industrial value chain:

• AgriTrust Exchange: a secure agricultural trade platform connecting African exporters with buyers worldwide, using escrow-protected payments and independent origin inspections.
• FactoraERP: an AI-powered manufacturing operating system that runs production, inventory, procurement, quality, supply chain, HR and finance on one platform, from intake to dispatch.
• Jengafy: an AI-powered construction platform for planning, estimating and managing builds, with cost estimates, Bills of Quantities, a contractor marketplace and project management.
• Purevado (co-founder & CEO): a Kenyan exporter of fresh avocados and cold-pressed avocado oil.
• CEA Consulting: a Nairobi-based investment consulting firm connecting African industrial opportunities with European capital, expertise and markets.

As CTO, my focus is the technology underneath these businesses: platform architecture, AI and data systems, and the shared infrastructure that connects the ventures.

My background is in computer science, information systems and enterprise technology, including roles in banking ICT and data forensics.

Outside Tamalaki, I'm also the founder of Playmefy and founder and chairman of PonaPal.

I'm interested in conversations with exporters, manufacturers, builders, investors and institutions working on African industry and trade.

Learn more: tamalakibn.com

What started as just a random idea soon turned into a creative deep-dive driven by curiosity — Flying Colors is my personal project born out of a desire to experiment with beautiful UI design and bring it to life using Flutter.

Flutter is an open-source toolkit by Google that lets you build apps for multiple platforms (Android, iOS, Web, Desktop) — all from a single codebase. And that’s where its power lies: efficiency, consistency, and speed, without compromising on creativity.

This project allowed me to:

Explore custom UI/UX design principles

Understand Flutter’s widget tree and layout system

Build responsive, aesthetic screens with minimal code

Think like a designer and developer at the same time


Flying Colors is more than a UI prototype — it's a creative outlet where code meets design. This project marks my transition from experimenting to executing with intent, and it’s just the beginning.

If you’re into UI, Flutter, or creative tech — would love to hear your thoughts or feedback!

posts.content:
Extremely Disappointed with Decathlon & Amazon Shipping | Unacceptable Customer Experience

This has been one of the most frustrating and disappointing online shopping experiences I have ever had with Decathlon  and Amazon  India.

I placed an order with Decathlon, but unfortunately, I never received my order, despite the order status showing as delivered. What makes this situation even more concerning is that the delivery partner claims the package was delivered with OTP verification, whereas I categorically confirm that I never shared any OTP and never received my package.

Order Details:

- Decathlon Order ID: 2636964536
- Amazon Tracking ID: 372635497662
- Order Date: 17 September 2026
- Delivery Status: Marked as delivered on 20 September 2026

It has been approximately 15 days, and I am still struggling to get a proper resolution.

When I approached Decathlon, I was told that they were not responsible once the order had been dispatched. On the other hand, Amazon Shipping claims that the order was delivered after OTP-based confirmation. Both parties are pointing fingers at each other, while the actual customer is left helpless.

My straightforward questions are:

1. If the order was delivered successfully, then who actually received my package?
2. If OTP verification was completed, where is the proof that I personally authorized or confirmed this delivery?
3. Why should a customer suffer because of a potential failure in the delivery and verification process?
4. Why is neither company taking ownership of the issue and providing a concrete resolution?

As a customer, I should not have to spend days chasing two companies for an order I paid for but never received. This experience has caused me significant frustration and mental stress, and the lack of accountability has made the situation even worse.

I am not looking for excuses, repeated assurances, or blame-shifting. I am asking for accountability, a proper investigation, verifiable proof of delivery, and a genuine resolution—either delivery of my order or an appropriate refund.

I request Decathlon  and Amazon  to investigate this matter urgently, review the delivery and OTP verification records, and resolve my complaint instead of misleading me between departments.

A company’s responsibility towards its customer should not end once a package leaves its warehouse. Customer trust is built through accountability, not by simply marking an order as delivered.

I hope the concerned teams will take this matter seriously and provide a fair resolution.

Decathlon  Amazon Fulfillment Centre and Service Provider

posts.content:
A year ago I joined one of the world’s leaders in ultra-luxury hospitality and gaming, with a great deal to learn about both.

At the same time, my family and I left India and moved to the UAE. A new country, a new culture, a new home, and all the challenges that come with settling a family somewhere unfamiliar. Professionally and personally, almost everything changed at once.

I brought 16+ years of experience in data, AI, analytics and product management to Wynn Al Marjan Island. What I didn’t bring was an understanding of what it takes to deliver an experience at this level. And here, nobody knew my past, which mattered less than I had assumed.

So I had to learn fast, alongside people who have spent their careers setting the standard for this industry. Watching how they think about the guest, how every detail and every interaction is designed, changed how I think about data. It stopped being about platforms and products, and became about moments.

Those early months were humbling. Credentials got me into the room, but they didn’t earn me trust. That came slowly, from listening before proposing, from working through disagreements, and from delivering on small things before big ones. Starting again, I realised it wasn’t starting from zero, it was a lot of unlearning,  learning and relearning. 

Since then I have been helping build the guest data foundation for an integrated gaming resort that hasn’t opened its doors yet, in a year when AI kept moving the goalposts. It pushed me to keep asking not what the technology can do, but what it can change for the guest and the business.

There’s one thing I didn’t get right: my own well-being. Between a new role and helping my family find their feet in a new country, it kept slipping down the list. That’s what I am changing in year two.

I am grateful to the leadership team and colleagues at Wynn Al Marjan Island for their trust, patience and generosity in helping me understand their world, and to my family for making this leap with me. I am looking forward to the opening and what’s unfolding next.

Growth should make life richer, not leave less time to live it.

author.about:
I build data and AI foundations, and the organizations that run them. 

For 17 years Ive worked on both sides of data: machine learning and analytics first, then data strategy, data platforms and Data & AI product leadership. I do my best work where business problems are messy, data is scattered and the path isn't obvious, turning that into trusted data, intelligent products and decisions people act on.

What I have done - 
Wynn Al Marjan Island: setting the enterprise data & AI product strategy for a multi-billion-dollar integrated resort being built from scratch. I lead a platform-first approach: one trusted guest view (Guest 360, Product MDM) reused by personalization, service, marketing and analytics, with AI turning unstructured guest signals into structured decisions. 

Diageo: ran a 45+ product Data & AI portfolio across 25+ markets. Built a 50+ person Product, Engineering, Analytics and Delivery organization, hiring 50+ people including Product Managers. Co-led a $65M+ Data & AI transformation, drove AI adoption in forecasting and planning, led the Stibo Product MDM implementation, and delivered £1.7M+ in savings and 25% faster delivery. 

EF Education First: built machine learning models for lead prioritization, market selection and marketing effectiveness. 

How I lead -
*Platforms over point solutions: build capabilities once and reuse them across many products. 
*Outcomes over output: products are measured by adoption and business impact, not by delivery. 
*Problem-first teams: I coach product managers and analysts to start from the problem and the evidence, not the requirement. 
*Trust by design: governance, data quality and explainability are part of the product, not an afterthought. 

Focus areas:
Data & AI Strategy · Data Products · Decision Intelligence · AI/ML · Customer & Guest 360 · Master Data Management · Data Governance · Product Operating Models · Snowflake · Databricks · Azure · Power BI

posts.content:
🚀 Introducing Infraji | Building Indias Construction Marketplace

I am excited to share that I am starting a new entrepreneurial journey with Infraji — a vision to transform Indias construction industry through technology, transparency, and innovation.Indias construction industry is one of the largest sectors of our economy, yet it remains highly fragmented. Finding reliable contractors, comparing project bids, sourcing construction materials, and renting machinery can still be complicated and time-consuming.

I believe its time to change that.

🏗️ Our Vision: One Platform. The Entire Construction Ecosystem.

Infraji aims to build an integrated digital marketplace connecting:
✅ Project owners with verified contractors
✅ Private construction projects with competitive bidding
✅ Buyers with construction material suppliers
✅ Contractors with machinery rental providers
✅ Customers with architects, consultants, and construction professionals
✅ Construction businesses with relevant financial and project-support services

Our mission is to make construction simpler, smarter, more transparent, and more accessible for everyone involved.

🤝 Looking for Co-Founders

I am looking for two ambitious, passionate, and execution-driven professionals to join me in building Infraji.
1️⃣ Co-Founder & CTO — Technology
🔹 Strong technical background in software engineering, technology architecture, and        product development
🔹 Experience building scalable web and mobile applications
🔹 Understanding of marketplace platforms, cloud infrastructure, and modern technology stacks
🔹 Ability to lead the technology roadmap and build a high-performing engineering team
🔹 An entrepreneurial mindset and a long-term commitment to the vision

2️⃣ Co-Founder & CFO — Finance & Strategy
🔹 Strong expertise in corporate finance, financial planning, and business strategy
🔹 Experience in fundraising, financial modelling, budgeting, and cash-flow management
🔹 Understanding of startup finance, unit economics, and business scalability
🔹 Ability to develop financial strategies and build investor relationships
🔹 An entrepreneurial mindset with a vision to build a scalable, sustainable business

🎯 Who Should Connect?

I am looking for people who want more than just a job — people who want to build something meaningful, solve real industry problems, take ownership, and create long-term value.
Relevant experience, complementary skills, integrity, and a shared vision will be important.
If you are interested in joining as a co-founder, or know someone who could be the right fit, I would love to connect.

📩 DM me on LinkedIn to start a conversation.Lets build something extraordinary together.

Infraji — Building Infrastructure. Building Technology. Building India. 🇮🇳

Are We Looking at India Through Yesterday’s Lens?

“Reasons to move faster, not to slow down.”

An observation by India’s Chief Economic Adviser,  Anantha Nageswaran, at our India Investment Seminar captured our discussions.

He was referring to geopolitics, shifting supply chains and AI. His argument was that uncertainty makes India’s transformation more urgent, not less.

Over the past two days, SBI Funds Management Limited and Amundi  hosted over 100 global investors from 15 countries in Mumbai, bringing together policymakers, economists and business leaders to examine India’s opportunities and challenges.

Capital follows opportunity. But long-term capital needs conviction, and conviction comes from understanding, not presentations alone.

As India’s largest asset manager, our responsibility extends beyond managing investments. It includes helping global investors understand the forces shaping India’s future. This seminar was the start of a continuing dialogue.

A presentation by a former RBI Deputy Governor was full of data points and one chart traced India’s higher growth trajectories over decades. Another projected a future in which India’s real GDP could surpass China and even the US.

India is among the world’s fastest growing major economies. What would it take for India to move from being one of the fastest growing major economies to becoming the largest?

Having spent much of my professional life in capital markets, I am accustomed to looking at growth, earnings, valuations and flows. All important measures.

Yet, as I moderated some conversations and listened to others, I wondered whether we are evaluating India’s future using frameworks built around its past.

AI challenges the technology services model that built India’s global success, while opening opportunities in products and intellectual property.

Domestic savings are changing the ownership of Indian equities, even as foreign investors remain cautious. Many businesses shaping India’s next decade are absent from established benchmarks.

None of this makes the projections inevitable. Productivity, employment, manufacturing competitiveness and execution will determine how much becomes reality.

Perhaps global investors need to look beyond today’s valuations to understand the structural changes underway.

Nageswaran’s observation was directed at policymakers and businesses. I think it applies equally to investors.

The India that could become the world’s largest economy will look very different from the India we know today. The real challenge for global investors is recognising that transformation before it becomes obvious in the numbers.

With special appreciation to Valérie Baudson , Chairman State Bank of India Olivier Mariée Debasish Mishra Denys de Campigneulles Vincent Mortier Elodie Laugel Gilles Cutaya Prashant Sarangi Moisendra Wala Romin C. Irani SBI Mutual Fund David ABEILLE Damarys Puel-Balas Seiha Lok Priyanka Dhingra Ernst Osinga

posts.content:
Asymptode is built in India, but every student we teach lives outside India.

People sometimes ask why we didn't start with the Indian market. The problem we wanted to solve looks the same everywhere: a student stuck because of a gap from a few years back, in a class that has to keep moving.

What differs is access. A family abroad often can't find a patient, strong maths mentor nearby at a price that works. India has many such mentors.

So the model is simple: one student, one mentor in India, one plan, taught live online.

It also makes some things harder. Time zones. A different curriculum in every country. Parents who need to trust a teacher they first meet on a screen.

We have built this without outside capital, and families pay for it. The next stage needs more than we can build alone, so I am now looking for the right early-stage partner, ideally someone who understands education and cross-border services.

If that is you, or you know the right person, I would be glad to talk.
